# Curio

> Ryan O'Connor's studio and free guide for people figuring out what AI means for their actual work. Four focuses to move toward, five fallacies that get in the way, a free 90-second quiz, and an on-site chat wired to Ryan's own working notes. Tagline: a guide for the AI uncertain.

Curio is teaching, not consulting. There is no funnel and no email gate on the
main experience. The chat and the quiz are free; two short Gumroad documents and
an occasional bounded consult exist for people who want more after they've talked.

## The four focuses

Whatever someone wants from AI tends to be one of four things. Each has its own page.

1. **Inspiration** (`/Inspiration.html`) — where this is all going. North-star framing, speculative thinking. "Stop asking what to learn. Ask what to become."
2. **Filter** (`/Filter.html`) — what to actually use and what to ignore. The missing thing is not information, it's hierarchy of attention.
3. **Mindset** (`/Mindset.html`) — for people already using AI who have plateaued. The problem is the question, not the skill.
4. **Solutions** (`/Solutions.html`) — help building, auditing, and thinking through a specific piece of work.

## The five fallacies

Five things people say to themselves about AI. Each feels like a reason. Each is a
fallacy, and each maps to one of the four focuses.

1. **Exhaustion** — "I don't have time." Expecting a tool that requires mastery. Claude doesn't.
2. **Guilt** — "Is this cheating?" A calculator was cheating at math, until it wasn't.
3. **Identity** — "I'm the [Excel] person." The tool skill is the ladder, not the destination.
4. **Muscle memory** — "Some day I'll be good at AI." There is no curriculum and no someday.
5. **Yesterday** — "I tried it eight months ago and it got it wrong." Today's model isn't yesterday's.

## Pages

- [Home](https://curio.help/): the cold open, the persona choice (for myself / for my team), and the compass hub holding all four focuses, the chat, and all five fallacies.
- [About](https://curio.help/about): why Curio exists and the experience behind it.
- [Quiz](https://curio.help/quiz): free, 90 seconds, no paywall. Returns your primary fallacy and a starter pack.
- [Ask Curio](https://curio.help/): the chat, on every page. Free, no signup. Answers in Ryan's voice from his actual project context.

## Who runs it

Ryan O'Connor — VP of Creative & Innovation at RedPeg Marketing, 15+ years directing
creative work at agency scale, architecture background, graduate-level teaching
background. He rolled Claude into a forty-person agency and reached roughly 75%
daily usage within a month; the same work surfaced about $433K in cost-recovery
*questions* (findings, not banked savings) by wiring Claude and MCP servers into
Excel, Asana, and NetSuite.

- LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/ryantoconnor/
- Substack: https://curioco.substack.com
- Portfolio: https://www.ryanoconnor.design

## What Curio is not

Not AI consulting. Not a course, cohort, or Discord. Not a YouTube creator brand.
Not a service treadmill. Not affiliated with RedPeg client work.
